blocks.text: Target Encoding deliberately covered the general idea and its real dangers first, disguised leakage from a row seeing its own contribution, whole dataset contamination, and severe overfitting on rare categories. Mean encoding, the specific, most common implementation of target encoding using the target mean, is where those dangers finally get resolved, through two techniques used together, out of fold computation and smoothing.

This topic covers exactly how K-fold, out of fold computation prevents any row from ever seeing its own contribution, the additive smoothing formula that blends a rare category own mean with the overall global average, how the two techniques work together to produce a genuinely safe, reliable encoding, how the test set gets handled differently once training is complete, and the standard tools that implement this correctly.
1. The K-Fold, Out of Fold Solution

blocks.alt: A held out fold gets encoded using values computed from the other folds

blocks.text: The core fix for a row seeing its own contribution is genuinely straightforward once stated clearly, split the training set into K folds, and for each fold, compute category means using genuinely only the other K minus 1 folds, then apply those means specifically to the held out fold. No row ever contributes to computing its own encoding, because the fold it belongs to is always genuinely excluded from that computation.

This is genuinely the same underlying idea as the cross validation technique covered in full depth in its own dedicated module later in this course, applied here specifically to solve this one particular encoding problem rather than for model evaluation itself.
2. Walking Through One Fold

blocks.alt: Four training folds compute an average target, applied to the held out fold

blocks.text: Concretely, with the training data genuinely split into 5 folds, fold 1 genuine category means are computed using only the rows in folds 2, 3, 4, and 5, entirely excluding fold 1 itself. Those computed means are then applied genuinely only to the rows sitting in fold 1. This exact process repeats for every fold in turn, so that every row eventually receives an encoding computed entirely without its own contribution.
By the time this process finishes, every single training row has a genuinely safe, out of fold encoded value, one that never depended on that row own target value at any point in its computation.
3. The Additive Smoothing Formula

blocks.alt: A raw category average blends with the global average into a smoothed value

blocks.text: Smoothing addresses the genuinely separate rare category overfitting risk directly, blending a category own mean target value with the overall global mean target value, weighted by genuinely how many training examples that specific category actually has. A category with abundant training examples ends up genuinely close to its own true mean, while a category with very few examples gets pulled genuinely much closer to the safe, stable global average instead.

This blending is genuinely what prevents the severe overfitting scenario covered in the previous topic, a rare category with only one or two examples no longer simply inherits those examples own target values directly, it instead receives a genuinely tempered, more conservative estimate.

blocks.text: 4. A Worked Example
Implementing K-fold, out of fold mean encoding directly with scikit-learn KFold shows the genuine, safe mechanism in practice.

code.content:
from sklearn.model_selection import KFold
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "city": ["mumbai", "delhi", "mumbai", "bangalore", "mumbai", "delhi"],
    "purchased": [1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1],
})

df["city_mean_encoded"] = np.nan
kf = KFold(n_splits=3, shuffle=True, random_state=42)

for train_idx, holdout_idx in kf.split(df):
    fold_means = df.iloc[train_idx].groupby("city")["purchased"].mean()
    df.loc[holdout_idx, "city_mean_encoded"] = df.iloc[holdout_idx]["city"].map(fold_means)

print(df)

blocks.text: Every row genuine encoded value here is computed genuinely without ever including that row own target value, exactly the safe, out of fold mechanism this topic is built around, resolving the disguised leakage danger the previous topic deliberately demonstrated.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Use a genuinely higher number of folds, 5 or 10, for a more stable out of fold estimate, exactly the same tradeoff covered in far more depth in the Cross Validation module later in this course.

blocks.text: 5. How the Two Techniques Work Together

blocks.alt: K-fold out of fold encoding and additive smoothing combine together

blocks.text: K-fold computation and smoothing genuinely solve two entirely separate problems, and both are genuinely needed together for a fully safe implementation. K-fold computation prevents disguised leakage, a row seeing its own target value baked into its own feature. Smoothing prevents severe overfitting on rare categories, regardless of whether leakage has been addressed.

A mean encoding implementation missing either piece genuinely remains flawed, K-fold computation alone still lets rare categories overfit to a tiny, unreliable sample, while smoothing alone does nothing to prevent the disguised leakage danger if the underlying computation is not also done out of fold.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: K-fold computation and smoothing genuinely solve two different problems. A correct mean encoding implementation needs both together, not just one or the other.

blocks.text: 6. Handling the Test Set Differently

blocks.alt: The test set gets encoded from the full train set instead of folds

blocks.text: The K-fold, out of fold trick is genuinely only necessary for the training set, since only training rows are ever used both to compute an encoding and to be encoded themselves. Once K-fold encoding of the training set is complete, one final, genuine encoding map, computed from the entire training set at once, with smoothing applied, gets built and applied directly to the validation and test sets.

The test set genuinely needs no K-fold trick of its own, since it never contributes to computing anything, it only ever receives the already finalized encoding map, exactly the same training-only fitting discipline followed by every other technique covered throughout this course.
7. Standard Tools That Implement This Correctly

blocks.alt: The category_encoders library implements mean encoding correctly

blocks.text: The category_encoders library, already introduced back in Binary Encoding, provides both TargetEncoder and MEstimateEncoder, both genuinely implementing smoothing directly, out of the box, without needing the manual formula to be written by hand every time. Combined with a manual K-fold loop, similar to the worked example above, or scikit-learn own cross_val_predict utility, these tools provide a genuinely complete, safe, and standard implementation.

Reaching for these established, genuinely tested tools is almost always preferable to a fully custom implementation, the subtle correctness requirements covered throughout this topic are genuinely easy to get slightly wrong when writing this logic entirely from scratch.

blocks.text: 8. Mean Encoding Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Mean encoding is covered here, hash encoding comes next

blocks.text: Mean Encoding closes out the genuine, correct resolution to every danger Target Encoding deliberately raised, out of fold computation for leakage, smoothing for rare category overfitting, and careful, separate handling of the test set. Together, Frequency, Count, Target, and Mean Encoding now cover a genuinely complete range of strategies, from simple and safe to powerful and carefully managed.

One genuine gap remains, categorical columns with extremely high cardinality, thousands or millions of distinct values, where even the compact techniques covered so far in this module can still struggle. The next and final topic in this module, Hash Encoding, addresses exactly that extreme case directly.

items: Mean encoding is the most common specific implementation of target encoding, using the target mean.
K-fold, out of fold computation ensures no row ever contributes to its own encoding, resolving disguised leakage.
Additive smoothing blends a category own mean with the global mean, weighted by its sample size.
Both techniques together are genuinely required; either alone leaves a real problem unresolved.
The test set receives one final encoding map, built from the entire training set, with no K-fold trick needed there.
category_encoders TargetEncoder and MEstimateEncoder implement smoothing correctly, out of the box.
